facts.label: Superlativos e passivo
facts.sub: Use the oldest / the most interesting para superlativos e was opened / was closed para o passivo no passado.

facts.label: o mais …
facts.sub: Use the + -est com adjetivos curtos: the oldest, the biggest, the longest, the newest. Use in com o lugar: the oldest school in town. Em happy, o y vira i: the happiest.

facts.label: o mais …
facts.sub: Use the most com adjetivos longos: the most interesting, the most famous. Não use -est com esses adjetivos. Exemplo: It is the most interesting school in Houston.

compare.ask: It is the oldest school in town.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “a escola mais antiga da cidade” e “foi inaugurada em 1890”.
compare.tip: Diga: “It is the oldest school in town.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use the + adjetivo-est ou the most + adjetivo longo: the oldest, the biggest, the most interesting. Depois use in para o lugar: in town. Para o passivo, use was/were + particípio: It was opened in 1890.

group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: It is the oldest school in town.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We say “the oldest school in town”.
“It was opened in 1890” is a passive sentence.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We say “the oldest school in town”. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “the most old school”. → Falso (We say the oldest.)
“It was opened in 1890” is a passive sentence. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: The oldest school in Houston · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a warm morning in Houston. Clara and Bill stand in front of a school. The red building is very tall. A big bell hangs in the tower. Bill smiles because he knows the place. Clara wants to hear its story.

“Clara, this is the oldest school in town. It was opened in 1890.” says Bill. “Wow, that is old. Was it always a school, Bill?” says Clara. “Yes, but it was closed for two years after a big storm, and the roof was repaired.” says Bill.
